suggestions.expectation: reply.md is at most 60 words, states what shipped and the first thing to do next time, and says the session stays open
suggestions.reason: The counting rule is unstated: `wc -w` gives 67 here, alphanumeric-token counting gives 64. Both fail this run, but a reply at 58-62 would be graded differently depending on the method; name the method (e.g. `wc -w`) in the expectation.

suggestions.expectation: Every read, review or verification that the session file's Outcome / Open at end / Narrative ... attribute to this conversation appears as a step in transcript.md ...
suggestions.reason: Good catch this iteration: the committed Narrative's `one commit ahead` is stale at HEAD while the reply says 2. Consider stating explicitly that `at leaving` state in the session file must describe the tree at HEAD after the handoff commit, so the failure mode (state captured before the commit that records it) is unambiguous to future graders and to the skill author.

No expectation checks docs/OVERVIEW.md, even though the skill's `end` procedure requires Status and Next up to match reality with the first thing next time at the top of Next up, and overview.diff is captured for exactly this. This run did it correctly (SES-006 Status bullet, ADR pass at Next up #1); a run that skipped OVERVIEW entirely would still pass all five expectations.

The `nothing stale found, nothing changed` wording in Open at end is contradicted by the same commit editing OVERVIEW.md. Whether handoff edits count as 'changes' is a skill-design question; an expectation could require that Open at end / Narrative distinguish review findings from handoff edits so the next conversation is not told OVERVIEW was left as found.

eval_feedback.overall: Expectations 1, 2 and 4 are discriminating and verifiable from the fixture; 3 needs a stated counting rule; 5 is the strongest addition this iteration and caught a real stale-count defect in the baseline arm. OVERVIEW.md upkeep is the one required outcome with no expectation.
